transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.
Next I'll compare per-service span volume, error share, and latency between the normal and abnormal periods.

input.query: SELECT 'normal' p, service_name, attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'abnormal', service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Frontend client and search client spans are much slower in the incident window. Next I'll check the status codes, span names, and the call graph between services.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, a.service_name, a.attr_span_kind, a.span_name, a.attr_status_code, a.attr_http_response_status_code sc, count(*) n, round(avg(a.duration)/1e6,1) ms, round(max(a.duration)/1e6,1) maxms, count(DISTINCT a.trace_id) traces FROM abnormal_traces a GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,4,1

content.text: The slowdown is isolated to `search` → `geo` (`geo.Geo/Nearby`, about 1.67 s client-side, while the geo server span is still 0.2 ms). `search` → `rate` is normal. I'll check the network-level metrics on that connection and the metric names available.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, metric, service_name, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*) n, round(avg(value),2) avgv, round(max(value),2) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*), round(avg(value),2), round(max(value),2) FROM normal_metrics_sum GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,1,3,4,5

content.text: This case has no per-connection `hubble_*` metrics. I'll look at the gauge metrics (`abnormal_metrics`) to see the resource picture for the services involved.

input.query: SELECT metric, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT service_name) svcs FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: Next I'll compare CPU, memory, and restart metrics per service between the two periods, to rule out resource saturation.

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT 'abn' p, service_name s, metric, avg(value) v, max(value) mx FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','container.memory.working_set','k8s.pod.cpu.usage','k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.memory.usage') GROUP BY 2,3), n AS (SELECT 'norm' p, service_name s, metric, avg(value) v, max(value) mx FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','container.memory.working_set','k8s.pod.cpu.usage','k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.memory.usage') GROUP BY 2,3) SELECT coalesce(a.s,n.s) svc, coalesce(a.metric,n.metric) m, round(n.v,3) norm_avg, round(a.v,3) abn_avg, round(n.mx,3) norm_max, round(a.mx,3) abn_max FROM a FULL JOIN n ON a.s=n.s AND a.metric=n.metric ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: Key finding: `profile` pod memory jumped from about 18 MB to about 770 MB, but profile's spans are fast and it does not sit on the `/hotels` path. The user-visible path is `/hotels` → `search` → `geo`. Next I'll check where the 1.6 s goes inside a search→geo call, using start-time offsets between client and server spans.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, c.span_name, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) client_ms, round(avg(s.duration)/1e6,2) server_ms, round(avg(epoch_ms(s.time)-epoch_ms(c.time)),1) start_gap_ms, round(avg(epoch_ms(c.time)+c.duration/1e6-(epoch_ms(s.time)+s.duration/1e6)),1) end_gap_ms, count(*) n FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id WHERE c.service_name='search' AND s.service_name='geo' GROUP BY 2 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', c.span_name, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1), round(avg(s.duration)/1e6,2), round(avg(epoch_ms(s.time)-epoch_ms(c.time)),1), round(avg(epoch_ms(c.time)+c.duration/1e6-(epoch_ms(s.time)+s.duration/1e6)),1), count(*) FROM normal_traces c JOIN normal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id WHERE c.service_name='search' AND s.service_name='geo' GROUP BY 2

SELECT 'abn' p, metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, round(avg(value),1) avgv, round(max(value),1) mx, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'k8s.pod.network%' AND service_name IN ('search','geo','frontend','rate') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, round(avg(value),1), round(max(value),1), count(*) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'k8s.pod.network%' AND service_name IN ('search','geo','frontend','rate') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 3,2,1

content.text: The network counters on search, geo, and rate are flat between periods, and the 1.7 s gap sits before the geo server span starts, while the response returns in about 1.5 ms. Next I'll check the logs, and whether `profile`'s memory growth reached any caller.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, level, attr_log_template, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, level, attr_log_template, count(*) FROM normal_logs GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, time_bucket(INTERVAL 2 MINUTE, time) t, round(avg(value)/1e6,1) mem_mb FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric='container.memory.working_set' AND service_name='profile' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 4 LIMIT 40

SELECT f.attr_http_request_method m, f.span_name, round(avg(f.duration)/1e6,1) fe_ms, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT t.service_name) downstream_svcs, string_agg(DISTINCT t.service_name, ',') svcs FROM abnormal_traces f JOIN abnormal_traces t ON t.trace_id=f.trace_id WHERE f.service_name='frontend' AND f.attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2

content.text: Profile's memory grew from about 18 MB to about 800 MB, yet `/recommendations` (which also calls profile) is about 0.9 ms. I'll compare profile's call latency to decide whether that memory growth reached any caller.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) ms, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,2) p95_ms, count(*) n FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name IN ('profile.Profile/GetProfiles','memcached_get_profile','HTTP /recommendations') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,2), count(*) FROM normal_traces WHERE span_name IN ('profile.Profile/GetProfiles','memcached_get_profile','HTTP /recommendations') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 3,1

content.text: Profile's memory growth did not change any caller's latency (`GetProfiles` is about 0.7 ms from frontend in both periods), so it stays inside profile. I'll run one final query to back the propagation edge from `search` to `frontend`.

input.query: SELECT f.span_name, f.service_name, round(f.duration/1e6,1) fe_ms, s.service_name AS callee, round(s.duration/1e6,1) search_server_ms, round(c.duration/1e6,1) search_client_geo_ms FROM abnormal_traces f JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.trace_id=f.trace_id AND s.service_name='search' AND s.attr_span_kind='Server' JOIN abnormal_traces c ON c.trace_id=f.trace_id AND c.service_name='search' AND c.span_name='geo.Geo/Nearby' WHERE f.span_name='HTTP /hotels' LIMIT 5
